scope: All 17 closed unmerged PRs returned by gh pr list --author @me; merged PR2406 excluded. Every current comment and review read. Read-only remote audit; no messages, pushes, reopening, test reruns or task edits.
method: Reasons are current official reviews. Critical assessment distinguishes submitted evidence from proposed changes. Six submitted README/task.json/task.py sets inspected at exact PR head: 2955,2906,2873,2871,2500,2544. Likelihood is qualitative judgment, not a calibrated probability.
recommendation: Prioritize authorized revisions on still-open tasks and stronger new candidates. Monitor the two already-filed appeals (2500,2544). Retire 2418 after explicit human denial. Do not send new appeals on current evidence. 2871 is the cleanest conditional unappealed candidate only if new evidence specifically establishes breadth/recognizability; available manuals alone do not.

prs.title: Unscrew a limescaled hidden aerator from a faucet spout with its key while holding the spout, then refit it flush
prs.rejection_reasons: Importance: hidden maintenance and covered hold/turn skill. Construct validity: aerator never becomes a free part. Scoring: arbitrary 1.1-turn removal threshold.
prs.critical_assessment: The submitted README admits reduced torques, fewer engaged threads and a taller key; task.py keeps aerator hinge/slider articulation and drives axial drop by angle. This corroborates rather than rebuts the mechanism objection. Real free-part removal/rethreading would require a new physical implementation and validation, not an explanatory appeal.
prs.transferable_lesson: Preserve real removal, alignment, thread engagement and access constraints; do not scale force or enlarge tools solely for the robot.

prs.title: Reassemble an electric carving knife: join the blades by rivet and keyhole, then click both into the handle
prs.rejection_reasons: Importance: specialized electric-knife blade assembly lacks broad recognition. Construct validity: latch insertion resistance absent. Feasibility: sharp blades with no specified gripper protection.
prs.critical_assessment: Published README explicitly says the latch cam is a rule and its insertion force is not modeled; a one-arm control scores 1.0 because the push is too light. This directly supports the rejected bracing claim. Hardware manuals establish existence, not broad firsthand familiarity.
prs.transferable_lesson: A disclosed approximation can still remove the defining physical work; benchmark the force-bearing mechanism before submission.

prs.title: Refit a pressure cooker's float valve cap: hold the loose valve in from the top and snap the silicone cap on underneath
prs.rejection_reasons: Importance: hidden float-valve maintenance is not broadly recognized. Scoring: concealed submillimetre cap/shank fit cannot be checked with ordinary tools.
prs.critical_assessment: No appeal filed and no fresh evidence in the discussion that overturns either objection. Pressure-cooker popularity does not establish widespread experience fitting its internal cap. A visible retention/function test might fix scoring but not importance.
prs.transferable_lesson: Choose an externally observable functional result; common appliance ownership does not imply common internal servicing.

prs.title: Snug a loose toilet handle: hold it level outside while the other hand turns the tank's left-hand locknut, not too tight
prs.rejection_reasons: Importance only: hold a handle and tighten a locknut is already covered; hidden toilet repair is not readily recognized.
prs.critical_assessment: No cited factual misunderstanding to reverse. Reiterating a left-hand thread or broad toilet ownership would not demonstrate a distinct manipulation skill or familiarity with internal repair.
prs.transferable_lesson: Unusual thread direction is weak novelty when the easiest valid physical work remains holding and turning.

prs.title: Put two coins back in an open kiss-lock coin purse and squeeze its ball clasp shut
prs.rejection_reasons: Importance only: coin pickup duplicates accepted piggy-bank task, clasp closure is a covered snap-fit. Flag: real purse stability and clasp force need verification.
prs.critical_assessment: No appeal or evidence of an additional coupled physical difficulty. Composing two covered operations does not by itself refute the reviewer.
prs.transferable_lesson: Novelty must survive decomposition into known skills and the easiest valid sequence.

prs.title: Press home a kettle lid left resting on its catch, without tipping the full kettle
prs.rejection_reasons: Importance: covered snap-fit, overlap with RoboCasa start-electric-kettle; unpowered kettle has no immediate safety decision.
prs.critical_assessment: No new evidence against direct benchmark overlap. A possible future scald after later heating is not a hazard the robot handles during this trial.
prs.transferable_lesson: Use actual in-trial consequences for safety claims, and compare against external task sets before building.

prs.title: Recentre a 17-inch floor pad lying off-centre on a floor machine's pad driver and click the centre lock home
prs.rejection_reasons: Importance: visible pad positioning and snap-fit already covered. Construct validity: removable lock becomes captive, driver detached from machine. Reproducibility: custom lock fixture lacks buildable drawings/equivalent.
prs.critical_assessment: Published README explicitly admits a captive sprung slider and code-triggered latch for a lock that the cited manual says to remove and reposition. Workforce count cannot repair loss of the real physical work.
prs.transferable_lesson: Do not replace free hardware with captive guides; preserve the host machine and access constraints; provide fabrication-ready reproduction when custom.

prs.title: Level a dishwasher's upper rack left higher on one side with its height adjusters, then roll it in to dock
prs.qualitative_reversal_likelihood: Low; relatively strongest unappealed case, still not ready
prs.rejection_reasons: Importance only: appliance-specific rack-height operation not established as familiar everyday activity or core work.
prs.critical_assessment: The submitted README cites Bosch and Samsung instructions describing this exact operation; these already establish reality but were available to the reviewer and do not establish that most people have done or closely watched it. No other criterion was rejected, making this the cleanest conditional appeal candidate only if genuinely new breadth/recognizability evidence appears. Repeating manuals or dishwasher ownership is insufficient.
prs.transferable_lesson: Distinguish proof an operation exists from proof of broad familiarity; prioritize evidence before implementation.

prs.title: Free a mug whose handle is cocked on a loose retaining rod, without dragging the rod out of its brackets
prs.rejection_reasons: Importance: loose rod through mug handles not recognizable. Construct validity: cited rack has a bar in front of mugs, not through handles. Flag: missing YCB mug license.
prs.critical_assessment: The rejection identifies a source-to-scene mismatch in the defining binding mechanism. An appeal needs evidence for the exact real fixture, not another generic mug rack; none is in the discussion.
prs.transferable_lesson: Compare source photos/drawings to the exact obstructing contact geometry before tuning a physically interesting invented fixture.

prs.title: Shelve a 1.2 kg steel tool tin whose lift-off lid only rests on top, without the lid coming off
prs.rejection_reasons: Importance: duplicate of accepted TK-5B8MZD, stacked-load transfer to shelf retaining loose upper piece.
prs.critical_assessment: Loose tin lid versus stacked box does not establish a distinct physical difficulty or success condition. No contrary comparison evidence or appeal is present.
prs.transferable_lesson: Compare physical success conditions, not object names or recovery framing.

prs.title: Move a ceramic tile left standing on its edge into a lean-to rack, letting go only once it leans on both posts
prs.rejection_reasons: Importance only: moving tile into supported upright pose adds no distinct skill beyond standing objects up.
prs.critical_assessment: No appeal or documented coupled constraint that defeats ordinary placement. Fragile material and rack geometry alone do not establish novelty.
prs.transferable_lesson: Analyze easiest valid solution and whether supports genuinely demand a new skill.

prs.title: Restore accurate weighing with a trapped grain under the balance pan
prs.rejection_reasons: Importance: diagnosis separable from ordinary pan/weight manipulation. Scoring: inaccessible 0.5 mm support alignment. Reproducibility: 3 mm salt cube and fault setup not repeatable.
prs.critical_assessment: Appeal fairly concedes scoring/reset gaps. Load-sensitive manipulation, released measurement witnesses and negative controls are legitimate implementation evidence, but Dream score zero does not prove importance. Cited Mettler guidance concerns another balance, while task is A&D HT-120; it supports general cleaning only. Proposed steel ball needs a verified real HT-120 fault and safe repeatable setup; it is not evidence the submitted task was misjudged. Broad lab significance remains inferred.
prs.transferable_lesson: Prefer observable zero/load/zero functional checks; validate exact-device reset and source relevance. Do not infer benchmark importance from model failure.

prs.title: Clear a cable-tie offcut from a Jetson controller fan
prs.rejection_reasons: Importance: exposed offcut removal is ordinary grasp/pull; Jetson label alone does not establish impactful AI-hardware service. Flag: third-party CAD licenses undeclared.
prs.critical_assessment: Appeal candidly admits simple extraction and missing licenses. Blade-intrusion and rotation verification add constraints, but NVIDIA fan-header documentation does not establish obstruction frequency or significant robot-building work. Proposed recessing of the offcut below the guard would change the task and needs evidence for realistic fault geometry plus new validation; it does not rebut the submitted scene. No frequency evidence is claimed.
prs.transferable_lesson: Safety/scoring sophistication cannot substitute for distinct core manipulation; source ordinary use and the exact fault, and resolve licenses before submission.

prs.title: Shut off a pre-rinse spray valve left locked on over a dish sink
prs.qualitative_reversal_likelihood: No further appeal justified by current evidence
prs.rejection_reasons: Importance: disengaging a locked-on pre-rinse valve not established as core for more than 500,000 workers. Human appeal denied Nov20 01:06:24Z.
prs.critical_assessment: Appeal transparently distinguished equipment prevalence and total occupational employment from exact-operation worker count. Human reviewer explicitly upheld the missing core-work threshold; repeating the same EPA/BLS/manufacturer evidence is not productive.
prs.transferable_lesson: A million establishments using equipment is not a count of workers performing the exact manipulation; human denial settles this evidence set.

prs.title: Re-chock two panes standing in a rack when there is only one prop block to hold them
prs.rejection_reasons: Importance/construct: miniature offcuts on artificial unstable strip do not reproduce sheet-handling hazard. Scoring: restoring starting poses clears prior fall/lift violation.
prs.critical_assessment: No appeal filed; there are multiple concrete defects and no contrary evidence. Scaling up or changing fixture would be a substantive different task, not correction of a misunderstanding.
prs.transferable_lesson: No miniaturization of the defining load/hazard; irreversible violations persist until actual environment reset.

prs.title: Straighten a stack of three cartons whose middle carton has slid out from under the top one
prs.rejection_reasons: Importance: duplicate TK-6NE9D8; setting top carton aside leaves ordinary stacking. Scoring flag: restoring starting layout clears tilt violation.
prs.critical_assessment: No appeal filed. Safe alternative is legitimate and collapses novelty; forbidding it would manufacture difficulty. No basis to repeat.
prs.transferable_lesson: Red-team easiest safe route and history resets before declaring a recovery task distinct.

prs.title: Reseat a board that missed one of its two supports, without knocking over the bottle beside it
prs.rejection_reasons: Importance: ordinary board placement and bottle protection do not establish human safety. Construct/scoring: held board up to 1 cm above supports earns full credit.
prs.critical_assessment: No appeal filed. Explicit scoring gap and weak importance both support rejection. A pending-review push was also explicitly ignored, emphasizing intake immutability.
prs.transferable_lesson: Require actual support and release; protect people rather than merely nearby objects; do not push while intake pending.
